title: Rare Event Analysis via Stochastic Optimal Control
abstract: arXiv:2604.13213v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Rare events, from biomolecular conformational changes and phase transitions to chemical reactions, are central to many physical systems, yet extremely difficult to study computationally because unbiased simulations seldom produce them. Transition Path Theory provides a rigorous statistical framework for analyzing such events: it characterizes the ensemble of reactive trajectories between two metastable states (reactant and product), and its central object, the committor function (the probability that the system next reaches the product rather than the reactant), encodes essential kinetic and thermodynamic information. We introduce a framework for committor estimation that builds on stochastic optimal control, with a principled formulation that grounds committor learning on capped hitting-time trajectories. translated_title: 基于随机最优控制的稀有事件分析
translated_abstract: 稀有事件，从生物分子构象变化、相变到化学反应，是许多物理系统的核心，但由于无偏模拟很少能产生这些事件，因此极难通过计算进行研究。跃迁路径理论为分析此类事件提供了一个严格的统计框架：它刻画了两个亚稳态（反应物与产物）之间的反应性轨迹集合，其核心对象——committor函数（即系统下一步到达产物而非反应物的概率）——编码了关键的动力学与热力学信息。我们提出了一个基于随机最优控制的committor估计框架，采用了一种有原则的表述方式，将committor学习建立在有上限的命中时间轨迹之上。在该框架中，committor定义了一个反馈控制，其大小与committor对数的梯度成正比，用于引导轨迹……
tldr: 该论文提出了一种基于随机最优控制的committor函数估计新框架，将committor学习建立在有上限的命中时间轨迹之上，为稀有事件分析提供了有原则且严谨的方法。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a principled framework for committor estimation based on stochastic optimal control, grounding committor learning on capped hitting-time trajectories to enable rigorous rare event analysis.
